utterances.text: I've explained that all decisions adopted by the assembly and later the Crisis Staff had to be signed by the president of the assembly or the Crisis Staff. And in his prolonged absence, and if the need arose to sign a document, it would have been signed by the vice-president of the assembly, but only during prolonged absences. Aside from that, all decisions were published in July, all the decisions adopted by the Crisis Staff, no matter if it was referred to as "conclusion," "decision." There was a list of these decisions. They were debated by the assembly and confirmed, accepted by the assembly, which made them official decisions. But this document, this order, for example, I'm not familiar with the content, but why should it be referred to as an order? That strikes me as strange. What sort of order? What is it about? I don't know what its content might be. There were a number of cases dealing with the use of weapons, expropriation of other people's property. The police failing to secure the safety of citizens and property. In such cases, there could have been but I don't know why an order. It may just have been a conclusion, on behalf of an organ within who's field of competence that would have lain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to stop you once again at this point of time as I mentioned before, we are not interested in the content of this special document. May the usher please leave this document with Mr. Baltic. And from Official Gazette Number 2 of 1992, page 39 to 40, the decision there mentioned as number 24. Is this the print in the Official Gazette of the document you just saw a minute before?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say, as I pointed out in a general sense, all decisions, all acts adopted by the Crisis Staff were supposed to be published in the Official Gazette. So it would have been normal for this one to be published there, too. Whether this in fact was the case, it may have been the case that those who prepared the Official Gazette for print did not include everything they were supposed to because they were supposed to extract this from the minutes and then control whole lists. And you have my signature, too, in the Official Gazette. There's always secretary of the assembly, president, this and that, because he was the one who was in charge of -- and as far as publishing is concerned, you have my name there. But mostly, preparation for print was done by one of the legal officers from the technical services to make sure that nothing was omitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Baltic. Could you please compare, on the next page, the number of the decision with the document you still have before you. On the next page, you can find... What is there? Is it the same number, 02-111-140/ -- I think it should read 92, Prijedor, 6th of January, 1998. Is this the same document?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm looking now at this document dated the 8th of June, 1992. And which is the document I should compare this document to? This is an order pertaining to whom I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please compare both documents you have before you.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've had a look. One of these decisions applies to a school, and the other applies to the regional Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do both documents have the same number?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. One of them has the number 02-111-140/92. And the other bears the number 02-111-136/92. So these are two different numbers. You can tell by just looking at the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. And if you could be so kind and have a look on the first page now of the Official Gazette, can you find this concrete number on this page? I think it was -- yes, the first page in the Official Gazette before you.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is from the Official Gazette, I can see -- this is page 39, and this is the continuation of that page, page 40. Official Gazette, 2/92, same number of the Official Gazette which means that they were both published in the same issue of the Official Gazette. It was said that it was those who made the text of the Official Gazette were supposed to list all the decisions from the minutes in the Official Gazette. Omissions may have been made but should have been corrected in the course of normal procedure. If so much detail was gone into, but I don't think much attention was paid to these details in the Official Gazette. Again, I say, because each of these decisions individually were forwarded to those whom they concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. If you, once again, have a look on the Official Gazette, you will find always "Predsjednik Kriznog Staba, Dr. Milomir Stakic, SR". What can you conclude from this?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can conclude what I've said already. In each Official Gazette, the procedure was the same. All the individual decisions published in the Official Gazette were not signed but merely it read the person, the official, the president of the Municipal Assembly who, by the statute, had the authority to run the assembly and therefore his signature had to be there, and his title, too. You can see this at the bottom of the page of each and every of these documents. This was regulated by the statute and by the decision on the operation of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Have you ever heard about an incident that one or several decisions were published in the Official Gazette without the underlying document authorising this publication?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to begin with, I think there was never a need to publish any authorisation for publication. This sprang forth from the obligations inherent in the statute. For all the problems debated at the assembly to be illustrated in the Official Gazette, to it was published regularly, again, I say, through the simple clerks, the lower-ranking clerks and the mid-level clerks. And it should not have been possible for the same decision to be published twice. I'm not familiar with any such cases of this occurring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did it ever happen that a decision was published without any underlying document? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, but such a thing should not have happened because everything is recorded in the minutes. Everything that is contained in the minutes should normally appear in the Official Gazette. If something else is published, then, obviously, it is a mistake. I don't know of any such cases, although it is possible. But I don't know how it would have been possible. We never carried out any specific control of the accuracy of the published decisions, decisions published in the Official Gazette, to see if they can be compared to what is contained in the minutes because that would require additional amount of work. I would have to sit down and compare the published decisions with the ones contained in the minutes. Later, if it is established that something was not published, then someone should be held accountable and see who it was who published such a document in the Official Gazette. But again, I have never heard of any such case, though I do not exclude the possibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask you to have a look on another document, on -- with the ERN number P0040716. Can we concentrate once again on the signature and the stamp. Here it appears to be a different stamp. Can you please explain what stamp this is.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, we can read here "Republika Srpska, Municipal Assembly, Prijedor." This should be the seal, the seal of the municipality. As you can see from other decisions, I am sure that there are other such decisions that bear the same seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Have you seen this seal before?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally, yes. But I cannot make out this one, but I mean, this should be the stamp in question, the official one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I ask the usher to present one other document, ERN number P0050275, to be put on the ELMO. Do you recognise this stamp?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As for the signature -- I mean, you're asking me about the stamp. This one is unclear to me. It doesn't look like the stamp -- like the one that I have just seen a moment before. It is not a very good reproduction of the stamp; it is true. But it doesn't look like the previous one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can you try to read what one can read in the stamp.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to, but I cannot see, for instance, the upper title. Because the right side of the stamp is totally blurred. I mean, the ink is blurred. If I am to compare it with the first one, maybe I would be able to make it out, the one that I saw before. No, I cannot read this one definitely. I cannot make out a single word on the stamp. It's unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So maybe it helps when we show you another stamp similar -- please, leave it with the witness, and then a stamp on the document ERN number P0012669.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For the record, that's S105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I thought it was sufficient, we all have this file of colour copies referencing before us, and it just starts with the list of ERN number and is followed by the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the stamp, I can see that it dates from a previous period of time. It is the stamp of the Socialist Republic of BH. At least, that's what's written on one side of the stamp in very small letters. But inside -- within the circle of the stamp. The Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And underneath, the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, and Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And then finally in our collection of stamps, Document P0038527.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That is S174.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I have a look at the stamp here, please. Good. I see the blowup. Yes, yes, I can see this stamp. This is -- I mean, I don't think that it is the same. It is a completely different stamp compared to the previous two that we looked at, on the document of the 3rd of June, 1992, and the 8th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind and read out to the record what you can read in the stamp.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The wording is clearly legible. We can all see it. "The Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Serbian Assembly of Prijedor Municipality."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. This concludes the list of stamps. And now, finally, let us turn to the document you mentioned, or maybe the document you mentioned already before. This is Exhibit Number S115. Please take care. That's the original. First of all, did you yourself prepare this document?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not my job, although at the bottom we can read: "Secretary of the Municipal Assembly, Dusan Baltic." If we go back to what we said before, that everything that was -- or was supposed to be published in the Official Gazette, then here we only have a list of the decisions that were adopted. Here, you have the relevant numbers and the dates. This can perhaps refer to the minutes, and we should have a look at the relevant minutes to see if these decisions are indeed contained in the minutes. And on the basis of the minutes, one can see what the chronological order was and that these decisions were indeed adopted. But I'm sure that I never did anything of this kind, nor at the Official Gazette. This was done by the people who took these decisions to the Official Gazette. We were only in charge of the document which is described in here, that is, the information. It is possible that the technical services did this, pursuant to somebody's request. I don't know who is indicated here as the addressee. The title is: "Information on the implementation of conclusions." What is meant by this, I don't know. It was impossible for the technical services to compile this. It was impossible for them to see whether these conclusions had indeed been implemented by the relevant organs. The technical services were in no position to obtain such information. I don't know why it says technical services here because technical services are not in charge of monitoring the implementation of the conclusions because the implementation of not only conclusions but also decisions, administrative decisions, they always state the organ of the person who is in charge of monitoring such implementation. It was not the job of the technical services to monitor that. They were not able to monitor any such implementation of conclusions. So this can only be understood only to the extent whether the technical services had actually distributed such documents. That was the only thing that could have been written and dealt with by the technical services. Technical services could only ensure that something was forwarded. But the technical services could not have insight in the implementation itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is indeed enough explanation. If you could please be so kind and try to explain how come we can find your name under this document.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said a moment ago that if in this so-called information, the relevant conclusions or the relevant decisions are stated, that is, the ones that the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor Municipality -- I mean, I didn't read the contents of this information. But as for the very title of the information, that is, the information on the implementation of the conclusions of the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor Municipality, that's all I can read. So the only thing that could have been stated was what was adopted at various sessions. And what was published in the Official Gazette. Whether those conclusions and decisions were really implemented, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, once again to interrupt, my question was do you have an explanation why we can find your name under this document?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: We read here "technical services" of the Municipal Assembly, and we can also read who the author of the information is. This was done by the people who were in charge of this job. I cannot see my signature here. It is possible that my signature is somewhere else, but I cannot see from this that I signed this document. But once again, the technical services did not have any insight as to the actual implementation of the conclusions and the decisions. But this is, you know, arguable.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone's off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Baltic, Mr. Baltic, I asked you on purpose this morning whether or not had you had assistants providing and preparing documents for you. Could it have been that members of your staff, if any, prepared this document for you and then it was signed on behalf of you or signed by you de facto? Because there must be a reason that there is here this document. One can say here as regards this document, it's signed by you, but it bears your name under the document which one would normally call a signature and the person doing so being held responsible for that what you can read about.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the preparation of all decisions that were on the agenda at the sessions of the Crisis Staff, the employees of the administrative bodies took part in such preparation. But I said that at the period -- during the period of time when the Crisis Staff functioned, since not all of the employees of administrative bodies came to work, only a limited necessary number of people came to work. If something had to be done, it was those people who were in charge of that. But in most of the cases, we did not have any written material in advance. Only on individual occasions, probably with the consultations with their superiors, the employees of the administrative organs would prepare such material. This was orally discussed at the session of the Crisis Staff, and the relevant information would be entered into the minutes in an abridged form. As for the wording of the very text of this decision, the employees of the administrative bodies were the ones who were in charge of this wording. Because it would have been impossible for them to be involved in each and every aspect of the problems because it involved a considerable amount of legal work. Something was discussed, orally debated, and then it was put in a written form in the relevant decision. The employees of the administrative bodies did not actually participate in this work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation. I think on this document, we got enough information from your side. But as you mentioned correctly before, we should draw our attention to the minutes of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly. And I have here before me a sample which will be immediately given to you, Document Exhibit S259. If you could have, please, a look on the first page and the last page. May it please be put on the ELMO. First page. If you could be so kind and read out the headline, say, the first three paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Abridged minutes of the session of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor held on the 27th of August, 1992 in the conference hall of RZR Ljubija. The session was chaired by Dr. Milomir Stakic, president of the Municipal Assembly. The session was attended by 72 deputies. Therefore, the debates held were valid and appropriate decisions could be reached. Before the adoption of the agenda, deputy so and so reminded the chairman that before the beginning of the work of the assembly, appropriate emblems of the Serbian Republic should be ensured."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And please, now, it's only limited time, let's turn to the last page, please. And please explain --

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've had a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. And then try to explain the order of signatures and your own observations as regards these signatures you can see there.

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since these are the minutes relating to the period of time which I could not precisely situate, I think that these minutes are actually the minutes of one of the confirmation or verification sessions of the decisions that had been adopted by the Crisis Staff. So this was all -- probably also published outside the Municipal Assembly, that is, in the Official Gazette. And that is why you read here: "SR Milomir Stakic." And then here, whether it was pursuant to someone's request. And in all of the Official Gazettes, if you have a closer look at it, you will see that the name of the secretary of the Municipal Assembly is always stated. There is a signature here. I cannot see whether it is mine, but it is not really important because this is something that would have been also published in the Official Gazette. This is merely the order of what had been presented during the procedure of verification or confirmation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you sign these kinds of documents in your capacity as secretary?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not necessary because no decisions are signed in the Official Gazette. It's not clear here -- oh, no. This is a copy because we can read here the sentence: "The accuracy of the copy is certified by..." So this was copied from the Official Gazette, and it was done by the technical services. And then the name of the individual in charge is stated, and in this case this was me. So this is just a copy. But it further confirms what I have already indicated. This had previously been published. It had already been contained and certified in the minutes. But the two were compared, and the person -- there was an official who was in charge of comparing these two and who is responsible for the accuracy of the copy. I'm sure we could locate such a person, but this was normally published --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You took the responsibility for the authenticity. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: That should have been the case, yes. Well, but if we can trust our own employees then of course, we're not going to read every single paper because that would take me forever, if I am to compare and verify Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. all of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So your testimony is it was prepared by staff members, and then you took the responsibility by signing these kinds of documents, and especially the document before you?

utterances.speaker: EDWARD SEBASTIAN VULLIAMY [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this copy -- I mean, I don't know why this was done in this manner because everything you can see here should be contained in the minutes, and I think that we would see this if we were to compare this document with the minutes. However, it is not customary for this procedure to be applied because if all deputies are to receive a copy of the minutes at the following session, they would -- they are able to see what happened at the previous session, and they are also able to point out to errors or omissions. Whether in this case there were omissions and then a request was made subsequently for a copy to be done, I don't know. I cannot remember this specific instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. My final question for today: Is it indeed your testimony, as you stated on page 105, line 2: "The accuracy of the copy is certified by... So this was copied from the Official Gazette, and it was done by the technical services. And the name of the individual in charge is stated, and in this case, this was me." So is it really your testimony that this was once again copied or once again written from the Official Gazette, first published in the Official Gazette, and then prepared in this way? I think you should think about this question until tomorrow. The hearing on the deposition to be taken stays adjourned until tomorrow, 9.30.
